Implementation Plan

I've read enough to plan. Findings: the four PR-item issue-creating paths are all in `scripts/unblock_actions.py` (`_fixup_ops`, `reissue`, `accept_with_followup`). `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` already fetches `pulls/<n>` around line 394 but only reads `base.ref`, `head.sha` and `head.ref`. The poller copies fix-up request bodies verbatim, so a provenance line placed there reaches the issue it files.

## Implementation plan: unblock judge never turns an untrusted PR's content into a new issue

Planning ref: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7` @ `b7c675dbb0afc480dd0dc93069153a54add133ef` (matches the integration branch metadata; no mismatch).

Answers applied:
- **Q1: A.** Fail closed at the source. For an untrusted PR, no replacement or follow-up issue is created. The PR is closed with a fixed explanatory comment and a Telegram WARNING. Issues created for trusted PRs carry a provenance marker. `clarify.yml`, `internal-clarify.yml` and the consumer templates do not change.
- **Q2: A.** The fix covers every PR-item path that creates an issue from model-written text: `reissue`, `descope` / `operator_step` fix-ups (`_fixup_ops`), and `accept_with_followup`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/unblock_actions.py::plan
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers set the scope: fail closed in the unblock actions planner for PR items, using the `pulls/<n>` response `unblock_judge.sh` already fetches. There are no new API calls, scripts, workflows or gate changes. Q2 A sets the breadth (every PR-item issue-creating verdict), so the plan neither shrinks below it nor reaches into the issue-open gate (Q1 C was not chosen). Under Boil the Lake, the fix-up request comment for a PR bound to a project gets the same guard. It is the same defect class, costs a few lines inside `_fixup_ops`, and adds no dependency or interface. Completeness serves correctness, which ranks above speed in §6.

### Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- No new script. Two existing files change: `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` (context build) and `scripts/unblock_actions.py` (op planning).
- Entry point: unchanged. The poller's `run_unblock_scan` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `*/5` cron through `internal-orchestrate-poll.yml`) dispatches `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml`, which runs `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`.
- No long-running supervisor is needed.
- No database work.
- No registry entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` is needed.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`: the context builder (around lines 384–426).
- `scripts/unblock_actions.py`: `_context`, `_fixup_body` / `_fixup_ops`, the `reissue` and `accept_with_followup` branches of `plan`, a new helper, and the module docstring.
- `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`:
  - extend the `_ctx` helper and the `FAKE_GH` `pulls/` stub;
  - adjust `test_pr_reissue_creates_replacement_before_closing_source`;
  - add new tests.
- `agents.md`: one sentence in the "Unblock judge (Phase 7)" bullet documenting the new marker and the fail-closed rule.
- `changelog.d/<this-issue-number>-unblock-untrusted-pr-fail-closed.md`: new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20).

No other files change. The poller's `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks` copies the request body (`$lines[2:]`) unchanged, so it needs no edit.

### 2. Functions / modules

**`scripts/unblock_judge.sh`, PR branch (after the existing `pr_json` read and `base.ref` check):**
- Read from the same `pr_json`, with no new call:
  - `pr_author = .user.login // ""`
  - `pr_assoc = .author_association // ""`
  - `pr_head_repo = .head.repo.full_name // ""` (null when the fork was deleted, which counts as untrusted)
  - `head_sha`, which is already read
- Compute `pr_trusted` with one `jq -e`. All of the following must hold:
  - `pr_head_repo` equals `${REPOSITORY}`. Compare ASCII-lowercased; GitHub repo names are case-insensitive.
  - Either `pr_assoc` is one of `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`, or `pr_author` is `${UNBLOCK_LOGIN}` or `github-actions[bot]`.
- Add these to the `context.json` `jq -n` call:
  - `pr_trusted` (bool; `false` for non-PR kinds)
  - `pr_author`, `pr_head_repo`, `pr_head_sha` (strings, empty for non-PR kinds)
- Log one line: `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item=<n> kind=pr op=pr_provenance trusted=<true|false> head_repo=<…> assoc=<…>`. This uses the existing `UNBLOCK_JUDGE` prefix, so no new prefix is added.

**`scripts/unblock_actions.py`, `_context`:**
- Accept and validate the new keys:
  - `pr_trusted` must be exactly `True`.
  - `pr_author` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*(\[bot\])?$`.
  - `pr_head_repo` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`.
  - `pr_head_sha` must match `^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$`.
- For `kind == "pr"`, the normalised `pr_trusted` is true only when the flag is `True` and all three provenance fields validate. A missing key or any malformed value means untrusted (fail closed). Values are never echoed into ops unless they validated, so a crafted login or ref cannot break out of the HTML comment.
- For other kinds, these fields are forced to `False` / `""`.

**New helper `_provenance_line(ctx) -> str`:**
- Returns `<!-- ai:unblock-provenance:v1 source_pr=<item> author=<login> head_repo=<owner/repo> head_sha=<sha> -->` for a trusted PR, and `""` otherwise.

**New helper `_untrusted_pr_ops(ctx, verdict_name) -> list[dict]`. It returns, in this order:**
1. `{"op": "comment", "issue": item, "body": <fixed text>}`. The text names the verdict (taken from the validated menu, so no model free text) and explains that the PR comes from a fork or from an author without write access, so no issue was opened from its content, the PR was closed, and a maintainer can reopen it or open an issue by hand. It contains no `reason`/`instructions` text and no line starting with `/`.
2. `{"op": "close", "issue": item, "reason": "not_planned", "pr": True}`.
3. `{"op": "add_labels", "issue": item, "labels": [CLOSED_LABEL]}`. The shell already skips this label when the close failed.
4. `{"op": "telegram", "level": "WARNING", "text": "Unblock judge closed untrusted PR #<n> instead of acting on verdict <name>; no issue was created."}`.

**`plan()` changes:**
- At the top: if `ctx["kind"] == "pr"`, `not ctx["pr_trusted"]`, and the verdict is one of `("reissue", "descope", "operator_step", "accept_with_followup")`, return `_untrusted_pr_ops(...)`.
  - This also covers `_fixup_ops`' tracking-request branch for a PR whose base is `orchestrator/project-N`. That request comment is filed by the poller as an `ai:orchestrator-managed` issue, which is the same laundering path.
  - For `operator_step` this also suppresses the operator-step entry and its Telegram message (both built from model text).
  - `retry_budget` (review dispatch) and `close` are unchanged for PRs. `auto_answer` and `override_guard` are already issue-only (`ISSUE_ONLY_VERDICTS` in `unblock_ledger.py`).
- `_fixup_body`, PR items only: append the `_provenance_line` as the last line when it is non-empty. The body stays model-text-safe because the marker is built only from validated fields. It is appended in both the standalone `create_issue` body and the tracking request body, so the poller's copy carries it too.
- `reissue` (kind pr) and `accept_with_followup` (kind pr): append the provenance line to the created issue body.
- Issue and project items are byte-identical to today.
- Docstring: document the new context keys, the fail-closed rule, and the marker.

### 3. Data structures affected
- Context JSON gains `pr_trusted` (bool), `pr_author`, `pr_head_repo`, `pr_head_sha` (str). This is additive. `_context` treats absence as untrusted for PRs. The shell and Python helper are staged together from one support SHA, so no version skew within a run.
- New marker `<!-- ai:unblock-provenance:v1 source_pr= author= head_repo= head_sha= -->` on issue bodies created from trusted PR items. It is for audit only; nothing parses it yet.
- No state-file, label-contract or ledger schema changes. `ai:unblock-closed` already exists.

### 4. API / interface changes
- No GitHub API calls are added. `author_association`, `user.login` and `head.repo.full_name` all come from the `pulls/<n>` response already fetched at `unblock_judge.sh:394`.
- The `unblock_actions.py plan` CLI is unchanged. Its context input is extended additively.

Failure modes:
- **Malformed `pulls/<n>` response:** already skips with `reason=pr_unreadable`. Unchanged.
- **Missing or odd provenance fields:** the PR is treated as untrusted. It is closed with a comment and a WARNING, and no issue is created. A maintainer can reopen it.
- **Comment op fails:** the shell's `ops_failed` skips the close (`prerequisite_failed`) and the label. The Telegram message is suppressed because the close did not succeed. The run logs `actuation_failed`, the verdict marker is already recorded, and a later scan retries within the existing ledger rules.
- **Close fails:** the label is skipped by existing logic and `actuation_failed` is logged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Treat untrusted PRs the same way for every issue-creating verdict
- Chosen: for an untrusted PR, `reissue`, `descope`, `operator_step` and `accept_with_followup` all become: fixed comment, close the PR, add `ai:unblock-closed`, Telegram WARNING.
- Alternatives considered:
  - For `accept_with_followup`, drop only the follow-up issue and keep the review dispatch.
  - For `descope`/`operator_step`, post a wait marker without a fix-up.
- Why: Q1 A says "creates no replacement issue: it closes the PR". Without its fix-up, a `descope`/`operator_step` cannot resume the item, and accepting an untrusted PR on the strength of a model verdict is the risk this finding describes. One fixed path also removes any model text from untrusted-PR actuation, and the item was blocked anyway, so closing it loses little; a maintainer can reopen.
